perspective:
From Keith’s available perspective:

- I work as a construction worker at the same company where Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist. We have a friendly but professional relationship, mainly interacting when I visit the office for paperwork or project updates.
- I noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with me over the past few days. I wondered if she was upset with me, possibly because of a misunderstanding or something I did unknowingly.
- I asked her if I had done something to upset her. She said no, not at all, and that she was dealing with personal stuff, apologizing if she seemed short.
- I felt sympathetic and told her I understood she was going through a tough time. I offered to be someone she could talk to and suggested a coffee break.
- She accepted the coffee break and thanked me.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; what she shared seemed quite severe to me.
- I thanked her for sharing and asked if she had considered talking to a professional, suggesting an external perspective could help.
- She said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- After I suggested professional help, I noticed she became slightly withdrawn. I thought I might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- I told her I hoped I had not overstepped and that I just wanted her to know I was there to support her. She said I did not overstep, she appreciated my concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- After our last conversation, she seemed more open and appreciative. I believe she values my support and feels more comfortable around me now. I intend to maintain this supportive relationship.
- I told her I was glad we could talk and that I am always there if she needs to chat or take a break together. She thanked me, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had my support.
